name: Code Review Practices (Overlap)
purpose: Content overlapping with existing code-quality-practices learner. Should trigger merge signal.
items: PR review policy: every change needs at least 2 approvals. One from a domain expert, one from a senior engineer. No self-merging even for trivial changes.
Code review checklist: correctness, edge cases, naming, test coverage, docs. Reviewers should focus on logic and design, not style — that's what linters are for.
Review turnaround goal: first feedback within 4 hours during business hours. If a PR sits for a day, it blocks the author and kills momentum.
Adopted conventional comments in reviews: prefix with suggestion:, nitpick:, question:, or blocking:. Removes ambiguity about severity.
Found that PRs over 400 lines get rubber-stamped. Team agreed to hard limit of 300 lines per PR. Encourages incremental, reviewable changes.
Review comment: 'This function does too many things.' Refactored into 3 functions: validateInput(), processPayment(), sendConfirmation(). Each testable independently.
Pair programming replaced formal review for complex features. Two people write it together, merge without separate review. Faster and higher quality.
Automated code review with linting: ESLint for style, Prettier for formatting, custom rules for import ordering. CI blocks merge if any rule fails.
Review revealed a subtle race condition: two async handlers reading and writing to the same cache key. Added optimistic locking with version stamps.
Added code ownership rules via CODEOWNERS file. Database changes require DBA review. Auth changes require security team. Infra changes require platform team.
Tracking code review metrics: time-to-first-review, comments-per-PR, approval-to-merge time. Avg first review down from 12h to 3h after making it visible.
Review patterns to watch for: magic numbers, hardcoded strings, missing error handling, N+1 queries, unbounded arrays, leaked secrets in logs.
Team retrospective: reviews are becoming rubber stamps. Solution: rotate review assignments, add review quality scores, celebrate thorough reviews.
Static analysis in PR pipeline: SonarQube reports code smells, complexity, duplication. Blocks merge if quality gate fails. Reduced tech debt by 30% in 3 months.
Pull request templates with sections: What changed, Why, How to test, Screenshots, Breaking changes. Reviewers know exactly what to focus on.
Code review anti-patterns: nitpicking style, blocking on personal preference, drive-by reviews without context, approving without reading.
Introduced architecture decision records (ADRs) for significant design choices. Linked from PRs. Reviewers can understand the 'why' behind structural changes.
Review found that error messages expose internal state to users. Standardized error responses: user-friendly message + internal error code. Details only in logs.
Pre-commit hooks catch obvious issues before review: no console.log, no TODO without ticket, no imports from internal packages, type checking passes.
Code quality dashboards: per-team metrics on test coverage, lint violations, complexity trends, review velocity. Teams compete on improvement, not absolute numbers.
Review comment templates for common feedback: 'Consider extracting this to a utility function', 'This could be simplified using X pattern', 'Missing test for edge case Y'.
Adopted trunk-based development: short-lived branches, frequent small merges. Average PR age dropped from 3 days to 6 hours. Merge conflicts nearly eliminated.
Code review for test quality: are tests testing behavior or implementation? Are assertions meaningful? Is the test name descriptive? Can the test fail for the right reasons?
Review checklist for database changes: migration reversibility, index impact, query plan analysis, data backfill strategy, rollback procedure documented.
Team norm: 'If you approve it, you own it.' Reviewers share responsibility for bugs that pass review. Changed review culture from checkbox to ownership.
